title: CLAUDE.md
text: zucbor R package encodes decodes CBOR (RFC 8949) ordinary R vectors lists, using vendored copy TinyCBOR C library system library required. CBOR JSON’s binary counterpart — maps, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, null — plus native byte strings, exact 64-bit integers, semantic tags (dates, bignums, UUIDs). Intended properties shape every design decision: Decoding accepts raw vectors, files connections; validates structure building R object; enforces configurable depth size limits, input expected untrusted (network, IoT devices). Encoding deterministic: identical R objects produce identical bytes. Target uses: COSE WebAuthn passkey data, CWT tokens, CoAP device telemetry, IETF protocols moved JSON CBOR. fourth self-describing format family zujson, zuyaml zuxml (sibling checkouts ../). design question answered , look packages settle inventing something new — ../zujson/CLAUDE.md ../zuxml/CLAUDE.md detailed.

title: zucbor 0.0.0.9000
text: Package skeleton: metadata, licence build configuration. Bundles TinyCBOR 7.0 (src/vendor/tinycbor), verified byte--byte upstream release tools/verify-vendor. zucbor_info() reports bundled TinyCBOR version, ceiling nesting depth default decoding limits. cbor_validate() checks raw vector holds well-formed, valid CBOR, RFC 8742 sequence, within depth, size item limits, without building R value. Duplicate map keys refused default, compared value. deterministic = TRUE also requires RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding. Every fault classed condition inheriting zucbor_error (see ?"zucbor-conditions"). cbor_decode() cbor_decode_seq() turn CBOR ordinary R values, whole-input check cbor_validate() runs. Arrays simplify atomic vectors elements agree; maps text keys become named lists; integers stay exact (cbor_bigint beyond 2^53); dates times become POSIXct Date. cbor_read() cbor_read_seq() read file, URL connection, never max_size + 1 bytes. cbor_map(), cbor_tag(), cbor_simple() cbor_bigint() represent values R native type . cbor_encode() cbor_encode_seq() write R values CBOR RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding: identical R objects give identical bytes every platform. Whole doubles written integers, COSE algorithm identifier written -7 stays integer. Decoding marks one-element array () keeps booleans apart numbers, decoding re-encoding gives back bytes.
